nodes.text: 1. Form 3 of Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure scheme will be enabled shortly

2. Due dates for filing of Income Tax Returns and Audit Reports for AY 2026-27 are extended in the cases of persons mentioned at Sl.No.2 in the Table below Explanation2 to Sub-section (1) of Section 139 of Income Tax Act 1961 vide Circular No.07/2026 dated 28th September,2026.
3. Form 1 under the “Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme” is now available for filing.
4. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, ITR-6 and ITR-7 for AY 2026-27 are available for filing through both online and offline utilities.
5. Filing of TDS/TCS Correction Statements pertaining to Tax Year 2026-27 has been enabled.

6. Demand Management Facilitation Centre (DFC), has been set up to guide Taxpayers on issues/grievances regarding their outstanding demands. DFC may be contacted through the e-mail id: taxdemand@cpc.incometax.gov.in or on the toll-free number - 1800 309 0131 or chargeable no. 0821-6671200.
7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

A  combines the flexibility of a partnership with the benefit of limited liability. It is a suitable business structure for entrepreneurs, professionals, and small businesses seeking a separate legal entity with flexible management and comparatively simpler compliance requirements.

An LLP is a separate legal entity from its partners, providing limited liability protection to them, subject to applicable laws. In India, LLPs are governed by the . An LLP can own property, enter into contracts, and conduct business in its own name.
Partners’ personal assets are generally protected from business liabilities.
The LLP has an identity separate from its partners.
Partners can structure the business and responsibilities through the LLP Agreement.
An LLP can be incorporated with the capital agreed upon by the partners.
LLPs generally have fewer statutory requirements than companies, subject to applicable laws.
The LLP continues to exist despite changes in its partners.
Partners can be admitted or their interests changed in accordance with the LLP Agreement and applicable law.
At least two partners are required, including designated partners.
At least one designated partner must satisfy the applicable Indian residency requirement.
The proposed name must comply with MCA naming rules and should not conflict with existing entities or trademarks.
A valid registered office address in India is required.
Designated partners must meet the applicable digital signature and identification requirements.
Designated partners require Digital Signature Certificates for electronic filing.
The applicable director identification number is obtained for designated partners.
Apply for name reservation through the MCA portal.
Submit  with the required documents and registered office details.
The agreement defines the rights, duties, contributions, and responsibilities of the partners and must be filed within the prescribed period.
Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and LLP Identification Number (LLPIN).
Complete applicable tax registrations and open a bank account in the LLP’s name.

Failure to meet LLP compliance requirements can result in additional fees, penalties, and other legal consequences. Late filing of statutory forms may attract prescribed additional fees, while serious or fraudulent violations can lead to further penalties or prosecution under applicable provisions of the LLP Act.
